title: 2026-11-05_UPSTYLE_Backdoor_Investigation_and_Response_a98
description: Investigate and respond to a UPSTYLE backdoor malware infection on a Linux system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has been compromised by the UPSTYLE backdoor malware. Your task is to investigate the infection, identify the malicious components, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) in the cloud sandbox using the username 'analyst' and password 'Upstyle2023!'
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) in the local sandbox using the username 'analyst' and password 'Upstyle2023!'

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the target host using the provided credentials.
2. List all services using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Look for unfamiliar or suspicious service names. In this case, the suspicious service is named `update.py.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl` commands to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual or unfamiliar names.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is not part of the standard system services.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Check the status of the suspicious service using the command: `systemctl status update.py.service`
2. Look for the ExecStart line in the service file, which specifies the command launched by the service. In this case, the port number is 443.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status` to inspect the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the ExecStart line in the service file.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified in the command that starts the service.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Timer
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers using the command: `systemctl list-timers --all`
2. Look for timers with unusual or unfamiliar names. In this case, the suspicious timer is named `payload-transfer.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with unusual or unfamiliar names.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious timer is not part of the standard system timers.
